runbook_name: SHS Operator Runbook V1 - Phase 6: Launch
goal: Document how a delivered project becomes a launched SHS client system.
entry_condition: Phase 5 QA + Delivery is Delivery Ready, final client-facing deliverables are approved or ready for final owner approval, report/public claim readiness has passed required gates, Production Ops has a final launch-ready project record, and open QA exceptions or post-launch watch items are documented.
exit_condition: ClientOps Active: final approval, launch date, client signoff, support tier, handoff notes, version launch record, ClientOps record, owner assignment, and open maintenance/watch item transfer are complete.

shrv1_surfaces.purpose: Internal/admin project status and launch handoff preparation.
Final project record context before launch handoff.
Development-ready packet and final implementation source context.
QA evidence, match notes, drift category, and delivery readiness context.
Trust-aware reporting/readiness context when reports are in scope.
Approval authority for public claims, report facts, readiness, and public approval.

shf_next_clientops_surface.purpose: ClientOps center for active records, maintenance, support, system health, version history, upgrades, monthly review, and exports.

bridge_context.finding: SHF-Next /ops/clientops has bridge entries to SHRV1 Agent Fabric and Reports governance surfaces.
/ops/clientops is classified as internal ClientOps for shs_admin and shs_clientops.

current_launch_context.missing_route_or_page: No dedicated SHRV1 operator Launch route was found in the audited context. Phase 6 uses existing Production Ops, QA, Reports, Truth Spine, and ClientOps surfaces.

operator_checklist: Confirm Phase 5 exit status is Delivery Ready.
Open Production Ops, project setup, build packet, and screenshot QA records.
Confirm final approval status and final approval owner.
Record planned or actual launch date.
Capture client signoff status and signer.
Assign support tier before launch handoff.
Write handoff notes that explain what ClientOps must know to support the client.
Create a version launch record with version ID, date, summary, active modules, routes, reports, known exceptions, and owner.
Confirm report claims and public claims use Truth Spine, Reports readiness, and public approval gates when applicable.
Transfer the final launch-ready project record to ClientOps context.
Transfer client name, business name, package, support tier, active modules, routes, reports, renewal or review timing, and approved operational context.
Transfer open maintenance tasks or post-launch watch items.

Keep internal sales assumptions, draft build packets, prompts, QA machinery, screenshot drift notes, blocked/internal defects, adaptive learning notes, sensitive client context, and unapproved scope decisions private.
Create or confirm the ClientOps record in the active ClientOps surface.
Assign ClientOps owner or support owner.
Mark the project ClientOps Active only after final approval, launch date, client signoff, support tier, handoff notes, version record, and ClientOps record creation are complete.

final_approval: Delivery Ready status is not blocked.
Client-facing content and assets are approved.
Report/public claim readiness is approved where applicable.
Launch date and support tier are agreed.
launch_date: Actual launch date is recorded after execution.
Launch window or timing note is documented if needed.
Owner responsible for launch confirmation is assigned.
Known constraints, blackout windows, or post-launch monitoring notes are captured.
client_signoff: Signer or client-side approver is recorded.
Approved exceptions or unresolved items are recorded.
Client-facing delivery note is available for ClientOps when needed.
support_tier: Monthly review cadence is recorded when applicable.
Upgrade or revision pathway is recorded when applicable.
handoff_notes: What was intentionally excluded is summarized.
What ClientOps must monitor is documented.
Open maintenance or watch items are documented.
Contacts, escalation path, and support owner are recorded.
Internal prompts, sales assumptions, QA machinery, adaptive learning notes, and unapproved claims are excluded.
version_record: Active modules and routes are recorded.
Included reports are recorded when applicable.
Approved exceptions and known limitations are recorded.
Support tier and owner are recorded.
clientops_record_creation: Client identity and business identity are captured.
Package and active modules are captured.
Support tier and owner are captured.
Open maintenance tasks and post-launch watch items are captured.
Monthly review cadence is captured when applicable.
Only approved operational context is transferred.

blocked_actions: Direct SHF Impact Data Spine mutation.
Bypassing Truth Spine, Reports readiness, or public approval gates.
allowed_governed_path: SHF Impact Data Spine only after approval

definition_of_done: Handoff notes are complete and private-safe.
Open maintenance or watch items are transferred.
findings: The launch-readiness audit states SHS/SHF V1 is private-beta ready with operator controls, but not paid-client or public-launch ready.
Existing SHRV1 Production Ops, Build Packet, Screenshot QA, Reports, and Truth Spine surfaces can support a manual launch handoff.
Existing docs define the lifecycle as Sales / Handoff -> Production Ops -> Development Library / Build Packet -> QA + Delivery -> Launch -> ClientOps.

SHF-Next /ops/clientops is the documented active ClientOps surface for portfolio records, maintenance, support tickets, system health, version history, upgrade opportunities, monthly review, and exports.
ClientOps is internal/private and should not be exposed on public SHF routes.
Launch and ClientOps activation are currently operator-enforced, not hard runtime gates.
launch_blockers: No dedicated SHRV1 Launch route or hard launch gate was found.
No automated Production Ops to ClientOps record creation exists in SHRV1.
No durable launch/version record backend was identified for SHRV1 Operator Runbook V1.
Client signoff, final approval, and support tier are checklist-driven rather than hard-validated.
Production auth and durable persistence remain outside this runbook phase.
post_v1_improvements: Add a structured Launch gate surface or model when owner approves runtime work.
Add one-click ClientOps record creation from a launch-ready project.
Add durable version records for launched client systems.
Add required final approval, client signoff, support tier, and owner fields.
Add governed ClientOps-to-report candidate intake when real reporting workflows require it.

npm run build.notes: Build passed with the existing Vite large-chunk warning.

npm run check:governance.notes: Master registry, proposal, Truth Spine, Oracle, AI Guardrails, Game Theory, data/governance layers, and duplicate cleanup checks passed.
